edition_scope: Publisher English Rules 2.0 (2016), complete base game, 6–12 players; no expansion or optional-mode assumptions.
review_type: Fresh independent source/key and coverage saturation challenge
blindness: Did not read the summary, reader prompts/responses, grades, or prior reviewer findings. Read the coverage ledger because the task explicitly required challenging its zero-addition passes.
method: Read complete OCR, directly opened the eight-page PDF with pypdf to verify the source artifact/page structure, and visually inspected all eight provided source page images. Used the images for text lost to OCR and the voting/Showdown diagrams. Checked every question and key, then challenged each core procedural passage and plausible uncovered boundary.

verdict.conclusion: The existing 27-question bank covers all distinct, source-resolvable procedures and outcome branches under the stated novelty criterion. Independent challenge supports the ledger’s two zero-addition passes. This is bounded saturation of the supplied booklet, not a claim that every reachable game state has a fully specified ruling.

findings.subject: Q24 normal refill
findings.finding: The answer is supported by the four-bars-per-round invariant and explicit retention exceptions, but is a procedural inference across passages rather than an explicit standalone refill instruction.
findings.action: No material key correction required; preserve the distinction if annotating source support.

findings.subject: Q27 outsider winner during tie resolution
findings.finding: The key follows the general double-Steal payoff plus the explicitly table-wide endpoint of the repeated tie Showdown. An outsider can win in the conditional scenario. The source does not restrict the winner to the initial tied pair.
findings.action: Retain the key. Do not invent extra-pot or multiway Showdown arrangements.

findings.subject: Tie Showdown logistics
findings.finding: The text requires another Final Showdown but does not expressly state how to furnish a new four-card pot for successive extra Showdowns within the same game-ending tie. Next-round replenishment language does not expressly cover this timing.
findings.action: Disclose when a fully executable tie-resolution procedure is requested; no invented gold supply procedure.

question_key_audit.reason: Visible matching IDs, matching Voting sets, unused colors returned to the box and hidden four-card pool are explicit. Own-color Ambush identity is legible in the page image although lost in the OCR.
No turn order, changes until reveal and simultaneous reveal after everyone selects are explicit.
Greatest total, not an absolute majority, establishes the Target.
All highest tied Targets die absent Ambush; voting for either tied Target qualifies. Page 6 diagram confirms plural Targets.
Non-Target votes cause elimination regardless of votes received.
Exact illustrated three-player branch: Ambush contributes no vote, Red/Yellow tie, Yellow dies, Red retaliates only against Yellow, Pink survives.
Successful Ambush eliminates one player who voted for the ambusher, not every voter or a nonvoter.
Non-Target Ambush self-eliminates.
More than two survivors continue the series of votes; only survivors remain standing for the next vote.
Sole survivor receives four cards; denominations are 3, 4 or 5 points.
Exactly two survivors must use the three-card sets, discuss, choose face down and reveal together.
Zero survivors awards one deck bar only to players absent from the last vote and retains the central four without new central gold.
Share/Share is 2/2 in the visual matrix.
Share/Steal is 0/4 in the visual matrix.
Grab One & Go/Steal is 1/3 in the visual matrix.
Grab One & Go/Share is 1/3 in the visual matrix.
Double Grab is 1/1 with two left; explicit note says draw just two new central gold next round.
Double Steal is 0/0; all other players get one from deck and all central gold remains.
End-of-round victory check, 25/24 thresholds by player count and highest qualifying total are explicit.

Repeated Final Showdown until any single player at the table has the highest total is the stated requirement. All return next normal round. The key reports the requirement rather than supplying unspecified extra-pot logistics.
Roughly ninety-second maximum, any overt/covert communication including texting/showing cards, and game owner requesting decisions are explicit.
Matching intended victim color, face down in front of voter, or Ambush instead of another player card are explicit.
Knock eliminated IDs over; only surviving IDs stand for next vote.

Normal replenishment follows from four bars available each round, initial hidden four-card deal and explicit retained-pot/refill exceptions. There is no isolated sentence directly saying to deal four anew after every fully distributed pot; label this as a well-supported procedural inference, not a verbatim rule.
Illustration explicitly retains Blue as Target despite protection and eliminates non-Blue voters. No promotion or retally occurs.
General tie instruction exists; only two sets and a two-player Showdown procedure exist. No multiway arrangement is specified.

Another Final Showdown invokes the general double-Steal payoff, and the tie endpoint expressly allows any single player at the table to become highest. Conditional outsider-win answer is supported. It does not establish missing arrangements for multiway ties or repeated extra-pot supply.

rejected_candidates.candidate: A successful Ambush against fewer or more voters, or with a different plurality margin.
rejected_candidates.reason: Q06–Q08 and Q25 already cover tally exclusion, protection, one restricted retaliation, failure and fixed Target identity; changed counts are cosmetic.

rejected_candidates.candidate: Two or more tied Targets all Ambush successfully.
rejected_candidates.reason: Applies the same Target/Ambush clauses separately. Ambush cards do not vote, so successful ambushers cannot be voters retaliating against one another. No new sourced priority or exception arises.

rejected_candidates.candidate: Successful ambusher chooses a voter who is already eliminated as another tied Target.
rejected_candidates.reason: Exact legal interaction is already shown in Q06, where Yellow is both a tied Target and Red’s only eligible retaliatory victim.

rejected_candidates.candidate: A nonambushing Target voted for another tied Target, or a non-Target got zero votes but voted outside the winning group.
rejected_candidates.reason: Q04 expressly eliminates tied Targets and Q05 tests elimination independent of votes received. Mechanical recombination only.

rejected_candidates.candidate: Three, five or more survivors proceed to another vote.
rejected_candidates.reason: Same continuation branch as Q09; counts do not change the rule.

rejected_candidates.candidate: Everyone is eliminated on the very first vote, so no absent players receive compensation.
rejected_candidates.reason: Q12 already specifies exactly the eligible set; applying it to an empty set is not a new branch.

rejected_candidates.candidate: An eliminated player reaches threshold from a normal double-Steal or zero-survivor consolation bar.
rejected_candidates.reason: Q12/Q18 rewards combine mechanically with Q19’s end-of-round check regardless of ending. Q27 already isolates the consequential tie-resolution winner-eligibility interaction.

rejected_candidates.candidate: Double Steal occurs repeatedly or tied players Share but receive different point values.
rejected_candidates.reason: Repeated application of Q13/Q18/Q19/Q20; no new source-defined ruling. Gold values are Q10. Do not introduce invented refill timing.

rejected_candidates.candidate: Exactly 25 or more than 25 points, ten rather than nine starting players, or different qualifying totals.
rejected_candidates.reason: Thresholds and highest-total priority are already explicit in Q19; numeric substitutions add no rule.

rejected_candidates.candidate: Reverse left/right players in an asymmetric Showdown.
rejected_candidates.reason: All six unordered card pairs already covered in Q13–Q18.

rejected_candidates.candidate: A finalist promises Share and then chooses Steal.
rejected_candidates.reason: Discussion, private choice, simultaneous revelation and Share/Steal payoff are covered by Q11/Q14. No binding-promise rule or exception appears.

rejected_candidates.candidate: Put Final Showdown sets aside during setup, enumerate all gold card counts or all character colors.
rejected_candidates.reason: Set availability/card identities are operationally covered by Q11; inventories add no consequential rule or outcome under the task criterion.

rejected_candidates.candidate: Leave the room to conspire or communicate with a different overt/covert signal.
rejected_candidates.reason: Q21 already covers unrestricted methods, including concrete examples. Another permitted communication method is cosmetic.

rejected_candidates.candidate: All remaining players choose Ambush; zero ordinary votes.
rejected_candidates.reason: Potentially material but not source-resolvable. The booklet never defines zero-vote Target status or how an ambusher fulfills the mandatory one-voter elimination with no voters. Do not assert that all die or all survive.

rejected_candidates.candidate: Select/discard/recover voting cards for eliminated colors or vote for a player already eliminated this round.
rejected_candidates.reason: The booklet gives no explicit round-to-round hand-recovery or dead-color targeting procedure. The defined participant flow is covered by Q09/Q23; a new affirmative ruling would exceed the source.

rejected_candidates.candidate: Resolve three or more qualifying tied players with a bracket, sequential duels or simultaneous matrix.
rejected_candidates.reason: An essential ruling is absent, and Q26 already tests that limitation. None of these procedures is authorized by the booklet.

rejected_candidates.candidate: Define who picks physical gold cards first, when received values become public or what happens when the deck is exhausted.
rejected_candidates.reason: No explicit source procedure. These are unresolved limitations, not valid answerable additions.

core_passages.passage: Visible IDs; matching voting sets and own Ambush; unused colors returned; hidden central four; gold denominations; Showdown sets
Series of votes; one/two/no-survivor round endings; zero-survivor absent-voter compensation and pot retention
End-of-round victory; thresholds; highest-total priority; repeat Showdown for ties; table-wide endpoint
Conspiracy approximate duration and methods; owner asks decisions
Target-color card or Ambush; face-down placement; no order; revisions until simultaneous reveal
Plurality and tied Targets; eliminate non-Target voters; standing/knocked IDs
Ambush excluded from tally; successful immunity plus one restricted retaliation; failed Ambush; fixed Target despite immunity; illustrated tied and plurality votes
Mandatory two-player Showdown; three card choices; bargain discussion; face-down simultaneous selection/reveal
All six unordered matrix branches; full and partial pot retention; deck compensation
Normal four-card next-round pot and special retention/refill branches
core_passages.qualification: Normal refill is supported inference across passages.

core_passages.passage: Gold recipients check totals regardless of ending; return every player next normal round and stand IDs

coverage_assessment.zero_addition_pass_challenge: Rechecked normal versus retained pots, first-vote zero survivors, all-Ambush/no ordinary votes, multiple simultaneous successful Ambushes, retaliation against already doomed voters, tie-resolution outsider wins, all six payoff pairs and the source wording of each action/transition. No candidate produced a new source-resolvable rule, explicit outcome branch or timing/priority exception beyond Q01–Q27.
coverage_assessment.saturation_boundary: Saturation excludes cosmetic numeric/color variants, component-inventory trivia, mechanical recombinations and invented fixes for omitted source procedures.

unresolved_source_limitations.issue: Three or more players tied for highest qualifying total
unresolved_source_limitations.essential_ruling_unavailable: How to arrange the mandated extra Final Showdown for more than two players. Only two card sets and a two-player procedure are provided.

unresolved_source_limitations.issue: No ordinary votes because all remaining players Ambush
unresolved_source_limitations.essential_ruling_unavailable: Whether zero-vote players become Targets and how to resolve successful Ambush with no eligible voter. No explicit ruling can be sourced.
How to furnish/replenish the four-bar pot between extra Showdowns when no new normal round occurs. The instruction to conduct another Showdown is explicit, but the supply timing is not.
Selection order among recipients, visibility of received gold before a victory claim and deck-exhaustion handling are not specified.
No explicit discard/recovery or dead-color targeting procedure. Do not silently add restrictions or consume/replenish cards based on assumptions.
